claims.text: Adding approximately 0.5–1 wt% yttrium to CoCrFeNi will maintain the desired matrix phase stability.
Yttrium addition will cause localized yttrium enrichment at the sliding interface.
Interfacial yttrium will enable formation of a coherent, continuous, adherent Y2O3-rich oxide scale.
During sliding, yttrium will react preferentially with oxygen to form a stable Y2O3-rich layer.
The Y2O3-rich tribolayer will dynamically self-heal or replenish itself during wear.
The Y2O3-rich tribolayer will reduce interfacial shear.
The Y2O3-rich tribolayer will prevent severe metal-to-metal contact.
Y-modified CoCrFeNi will have a lower coefficient of friction than undoped CoCrFeNi from room temperature through 800 °C.
Y-modified CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate than undoped CoCrFeNi from room temperature through 800 °C.
The beneficial tribological effects will persist under moderate-to-high sliding loads typical of the proposed tests.
The intervention will maintain low friction and wear under varying environmental conditions, including ambient oxidizing and controlled atmospheres.
At temperatures significantly above 800 °C, the Y2O3-rich tribolayer may lose formation capability or stability.
At extreme loads, the Y2O3-rich tribolayer may lose formation capability or stability.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field describes failure using the conjunction of absent Y2O3 tribolayer formation and baseline-like performance, whereas the formal falsification rule treats either absent performance improvement or absent tribolayer formation as independently sufficient.
